title: Receipt OCR to structured JSON
business_story: Expense-management and bookkeeping tools turn photographed receipts into ledger entries; after OCR the text is jumbled, and a model has to pull out the line items and totals for every receipt a customer uploads. It runs once per document at high volume, so the per-call price decides the margin.
instruction:
The text below is the OCR output of a shop or restaurant receipt from Indonesia (amounts in rupiah). Extract the following as a JSON object and reply with the JSON only:
- "items": the purchased line items, each {"name": string as printed, "quantity": integer or null, "price": the line total as printed, integer}. Do not list sub-items or modifiers printed under an item.
- "subtotal", "discount", "service_charge", "tax", "total", "cash_paid", "change": integers, or null if the receipt does not print that amount.
Write every amount as a plain integer with no currency or separators ("Rp 25.000" -> 25000). Discounts are positive numbers.
attribution: Park et al., 'CORD: A Consolidated Receipt Dataset for Post-OCR Parsing', 2019. NAVER Clova.
split_note: input is the dataset's own OCR words regrouped into lines by row_id; reference built from gt_parse. Receipts with ambiguous amounts, an item without a line total, or nested multi-value fields were dropped. Holdout is every usable receipt in the test split; tuning and validation rows come from the validation split (the rows API does not serve the train split).
